signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Energy Outperformance
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard confirms severe cross-sectional divergence, with NOK gaining +0.814% across its G10 pairs over the last week while EUR lags at -0.539% across nine pairs. The resulting 1.353% leader-to-laggard spread triggers a critical bilateral theme signal. NOK is directly supported by WTI crude hovering near $89.0/bbl amid ongoing Middle East transit disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Conversely, EUR is weighed down by a negative rate differential and weak economic momentum. Trade bias: Long NOK/EUR, exploiting broad G10 energy and policy divergence. Catalyst: Germany Trade Balance data release at 06:00 UTC. Risk: A sharp retracement in crude oil prices compresses the bilateral spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.09, positioned above its SMA20 (156.64) and SMA50 (157.79) but capped below the SMA200 at 158.50. The 275bp Fed-BoJ policy rate spread (SOFR 3.89% vs TONA 1.23% yielding +266bp OIS) continues to anchor carry demand for the dollar. However, FX options reflect strong downside hedging demand, with 25-delta Risk Reversals at -1.94 and 1M IV at 8.2% trading below 30-day realized volatility at 9.8% (VRP -1.6%). CFTC Leveraged Funds net short JPY at -16,809 contracts (96th percentile) confirms carry positioning remains heavily crowded. While 160.00 remains the key level that previously triggered BoJ verbal warnings, current VIX levels at 15.1 keep carry intact until market volatility escalates. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carried by yield differentials while volatility remains subdued. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims release at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Break above 160.00 sparks fresh intervention risk or a spike in VIX forces carry unwinds.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Squeeze + Retail Extreme
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1199, breaking below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.1426/1.1524/1.1608). The Fed-ECB policy differential of 135bp in favor of USD continues to pressure the single currency. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds extending net short positions to -82,445 contracts (6th percentile of its 52-week range), while Retail sentiment data retail sentiment is extremely stretched at 85% long. Options pricing indicates high protection demand, with 1M IV at 6.7% vs HV30 at 3.9% generating an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.9%. This multi-layer divergence between institutional net short flows and retail net long conviction signals downside continuation with squeeze volatility. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, driven by policy spreads and retail positioning divergence. Catalyst: ECB Monetary Policy Meeting Accounts release at 11:30 UTC. Risk: US Initial Jobless Claims miss expectations, forcing a short-covering rally back above 1.1264.

signals.title: USD/CAD — COT vs Real Yield Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD holds at 1.4259, comfortably above its SMA20 (1.4063), SMA50 (1.3964), and SMA200 (1.3859). A 175bp Fed-BoC rate differential (SOFR 3.89% vs CORRA 2.29% yielding +160bp OIS) supports the pair. US 5Y real yields have expanded +53bp over 20 sessions (FRED, as of Oct 05), bolstering broad dollar strength against CAD's positive Economic Surprise Index (+15.1). CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a substantial net short in CAD at -72,519 contracts, but Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows an extreme 96% short bias on USD/CAD. The combination of strong real yield support and retail fading the trend supports ongoing upward momentum. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, supported by real yield differentials and retail contrarian flows. Catalyst: Canada Employment Change report at 12:30 UTC. Risk: A stronger-than-expected Canadian jobs report triggers unwinds of speculative short CAD positions.
